title: OC Nathaniel Hackett Press Conference | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Hackett won't rush rookie RB Jeremiyah Love back and is happy with a three-man backfield of Love, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier, while Jacoby Brissett has a dedicated short-yardage package.
summary: Hackett was asked how he will juggle the backfield once Jeremiyah Love can play again. He said he wants to get the ball to all of Love, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier, and he praised Knight for taking advantage of his chance. He gave no split of touches. On the question of getting Love more involved in the passing game, he said the focus is purely on getting Love healthy before anything else. He did not name an injury or give a return timeline. On short yardage, he said the team has built a package specific to Jacoby Brissett, who is good at sneaks. They will mix shotgun and under-center looks so defenses can't predict a sneak every time. Asked about the league-high rate of three-and-outs, he said it comes down to small things like a face-mask penalty and minor breakdowns on manageable third downs. He said drives that do get a first down tend to go long. He said Michael Wilson has been targeted a lot, is near the top in receptions and has been close to explosive plays on 50/50 balls. The plan is to keep giving him opportunities. He added that Wilson is new to the building and still learning the system, and that he brings veteran presence. He closed with praise for Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

injuries.detail: Missed the last couple of games. Hackett said the focus is getting him healthy and gave no timeline or injury details. He is not on this week's injury report.

signals.claim: Love's return and any expanded role, including more passing-game work, depend on him getting healthy first.
signals.note: Hackett is not committing to a return date or a bigger role, so Love's availability and workload remain uncertain.
signals.quote: keep giving him the ball.

signals.claim: Knight will remain part of a three-man backfield rotation when Love returns.
signals.note: Knight has played well in Love's absence, but a returning Love could cut into his touches, and Knight is on the injury report with a concussion.
signals.quote: He took advantage of his opportunity.

signals.claim: Allgeier stays in the backfield mix with Love and Knight.
signals.note: Hackett wants to use all three backs, which points to a committee with no clear lead back.
signals.quote: very happy to have all three.

signals.claim: Arizona will keep using a package built around Brissett for third-and-short and fourth-and-short, including sneaks.
signals.note: A designed short-yardage role for the QB can mean goal-line and short-yardage rushing production, and it takes some of those carries away from the RBs.
signals.quote: we built a nice little package that's specific to him.

signals.claim: Wilson will keep getting targets, including deep and 50/50 balls.
signals.note: Steady targets and near-miss explosive plays make him a possible breakout candidate, although Hackett gave no concrete usage change.
signals.quote: He's been very close a couple times.

topics.detail: Hackett said Arizona has one of the league's highest three-and-out rates. He blamed small things such as a face-mask penalty and minor breakdowns on manageable third downs rather than a broad problem. He said that when the offense gets a first down, it tends to produce long drives.

The offense mixes shotgun and under-center looks on third and fourth and short. It keeps the threat of a pass while still running downhill. Because Brissett is good at sneaks, the package is built around him.
Hackett spoke respectfully of Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer, whom he has known since childhood through their coaching families. He said Schottenheimer runs an old West Coast style.
Hackett said veteran receivers can sometimes start immediately and sometimes need more time. He said Wilson is bringing veteran presence and a good personality, and is learning the system.

title: Jeff Ulbrich, Tommy Rees & Craig Aukerman on preparation for Falcons vs Buccaneers matchup | Press Conference
headline: Tommy Rees offered no role or injury news; he praised Michael Penix Jr.'s poise after a comeback from 14-3 down and stressed ball security against peanut punches.
summary: Only a portion of this shared press conference is Rees. The rest is the defensive and special-teams coordinators, whose comments are left out here. Rees said he and the staff are focused week to week and not on development benchmarks for Penix, who just made his 17th career start and was NFC Offensive Player of the Week. He said the offense still wants to improve and to magnify what Penix does well. He called Penix's poise a major strength and said his quiet demeanor hides a fierce competitor, pointing to the comeback after trailing 14-3. He described the quarterback-play-caller relationship as open: he won't call a play Penix doesn't believe in, and a player's objection takes it out of the plan. On the peanut-punch theme, he said defenders are so good at stripping the ball that the offense drills ball security every week, and he singled out Drake London's strength carrying defenders down to the five. He discussed the hook-and-lateral trick play, which Chicago ran on Atlanta and Buffalo has used in key moments, and said it is a situational call with limited risk. He also described a smooth, collaborative game-day relationship with Kevin Stefanski and owned his sideline intensity and the viral camera clips. He said nothing about the Buccaneers' defense, injuries or any depth-chart or usage changes.

signals.claim: Penix keeps playing at a high level and the offense is looking to build on his recent sustained success.
signals.note: The OC's confidence in Penix's poise and preparation supports his steady QB production after the comeback win.
signals.quote: He was unflappable.

signals.note: Rees held up London's physical, secure play after the catch over the middle as the model for ball security, a sign of trust in his role.
signals.quote: He's dragging two guys with him.

topics.detail: Defenders are getting so good at punching the ball out that the offense drills ball security every week, with Coach Petrie leading it and Stefanski showing film clips to the team.

Rees said it is a situational play the team keeps available and runs only against certain looks, which limits the risk. Chicago ran it on Atlanta a couple of weeks ago and Buffalo has used it in critical third-and-long spots.
Rees wants Penix to have full belief in every call and says a call Penix isn't comfortable with comes out of the plan. He credited the QB room's good vibes and said Tua has been supportive.

Most of the game plan is settled during the week with Stefanski. On game day Stefanski mainly steers game-management situations, such as end-of-half and end-of-game handling, rather than dictating specific plays.
Rees acknowledged his intense sideline reactions, including the old Notre Dame clip, said he needs to be more aware of the cameras, and said he won't change who he is.

title: Declan Doyle Discusses Second-Half Adjustments
headline: Lamar Jackson may return this week, but Doyle gave no confirmation. Offense is trying to fix its second-half scoring drought and a struggling run game.
summary: Doyle took ownership of the offense's scoreless second halves over the past couple of weeks, saying the backup quarterback is not an excuse. He said he spends as much time on the second-half script as on the opening script, but he hasn't stuck with it enough and needs to trust his calls more. The tape shows the offense not executing what is called, and the staff is reviewing the process, the halftime meetings and how information reaches the players. He called the run game's problems a matter of many small details: communication on the offensive line leaves unblocked defenders unaccounted for, and tight ends, receivers, backs and the quarterback all have to clean up their roles. He said the offense will simplify and cut variables when things go wrong, and will never abandon the run. On Lamar Jackson, he said he is excited if Jackson is back this week, and the staff is making practice and walkthroughs as game-like as possible after the layoff. He credited Tyler Huntley (Snoop) with creating some plays on his own, praised Cam Jurgens in his first game at center, and called Josh Allen an outstanding player ahead of the matchup with Buffalo.

injuries.detail: Has missed a few weeks. Doyle said he is 'excited if he's back this week' but gave no firm confirmation. The staff is simulating game-like reps in practice to avoid rust.

signals.claim: Jackson may return to the lineup this week
signals.note: His return would restore the offense's top playmaker, but Doyle did not confirm it, so his availability needs monitoring.
signals.quote: I'm certainly excited if he's back this week and we're rolling with him.

signals.claim: Huntley has been the starter in the games without Jackson and would go back to the bench if Jackson returns
signals.note: Doyle credited him with creating some plays on his own, but his fantasy value depends on Jackson's status.
signals.quote: Snoop has been able to create a little bit as well on his own.

signals.claim: Jurgens played center in his first game there and graded well
signals.note: Positive review of the interior line shift, though the run game still has communication problems.
signals.quote: cam did an awesome job in the game

topics.detail: The offense has scored no second-half points in recent weeks. Doyle blamed execution and his own sticking with the script, and said he is reworking the halftime process and how calls are communicated.

Yards before contact are shrinking because of missed assignments and unblocked defenders. He wants cleaner communication across the line and better blocking from tight ends and wideouts, and said they will not abandon the run.

Doyle scripts openers and a second-half script, plus ranked calls by situation reviewed with the quarterbacks. He described 'get back on track' plays as calls for second-and-7 or longer. He is in his first season as play caller and seven games in.
From the booth he only has direct contact with the quarterback and staff, so the message to players has to flow through them.
Doyle praised Allen's arm talent and the Bills' offense (OC Pete Carmichael) and said he is excited for Baltimore's defense to face them.

title: OC Davis Webb on Denver’s success vs. Cardinals: ‘We are just building off of that’
headline: Webb says the RB work is week to week with Jonah Coleman healthy and hot late, and Marvin Mims Jr. is 'involved' but the ball hasn't found him.
summary: Webb said the offense went back to the Week 1 loss to Kansas City and the film showed execution and play-calling errors in a game that stayed within a score into the second half. He credited the Arizona win to a screen play, another big play, better running and a big Bo Nix run, and wants to stack good weeks. On the three-man backfield, he said last week several backs got opportunities. RJ Harvey had some pass-game work, a starter opened the game, and Jonah Coleman got hot and finished it. He called the split week to week and said Sunday's game will decide how it plays out. Asked about getting Marvin Mims Jr. more touches, he said Mims has been involved, but the ball hasn't found him because of protection or coverage, and that the offense tends to do well when Mims is hot. He praised Kansas City's defensive coordinator as one of the best he has coached and said the run game is close to dominating the line of scrimmage, with runners reaching the second and third levels and wearing teams down for a strong fourth quarter. He also said Nix contributes ideas to the game plan but is not in the coaches' meetings.

injuries.detail: The question described him as back healthy and coming on; Webb did not dispute this, and he was used heavily late last game.

signals.claim: Coleman will keep a meaningful share of the RB work, as he finished last week's game as the lead back.
signals.note: He got hot and was ridden late, so he is trending up in a crowded three-back committee, but Webb says the split is week to week.
signals.quote: then Jonah kind of got hot and then kind of road Jonah at the end.

signals.claim: Harvey will keep some pass-game work in the RB rotation.
signals.note: His role looks tied to the passing game in a committee, so his weekly volume is uncertain.
signals.quote: Obviously, RJ had the pass game a little bit

signals.claim: Mims is already involved in the game plan, but targets depend on protection and coverage.
signals.note: Payton wants him more involved, but Webb did not promise a bigger role, so his target volume stays volatile and big-play dependent.
signals.quote: I just don't know if the balls found him necessarily.

signals.claim: Nix contributes ideas to the game plan and had a big run against Arizona.
signals.note: His rushing production adds to his fantasy floor, and Webb is open to his input on the plan.
signals.quote: he definitely shoots his ideas.

topics.detail: Webb said the team revisited the Week 1 loss, which he blamed on a few execution and play-calling errors, and noted the game was within a score into the second half. The Colts game a few weeks later was another back-and-forth example.
He wants the line to dominate the line of scrimmage so runners reach the second and third levels. He said the team wears opponents down and is 'getting close' to exploding in the fourth quarter.
Webb called the Chiefs' defensive coordinator one of the best he has coached. He said the unit is good at taking away your best player and disguising how to beat the protections.

title: Petzing on run game
headline: Petzing won't cap Jahmyr Gibbs' touches and calls the run game key against Flores' Vikings; Jameson Williams praised and Cade Mays' debut called a 'really good start'.
summary: Petzing spent most of the session on Brian Flores' Minnesota defense. He called it a unique system with identical pre-snap looks, and said the key is keeping Minnesota off balance with a mix of run and pass. He said the run game has been inconsistent, with explosive plays offset by negative ones, and blamed protection ID and communication, losing one-on-ones, and occasionally play-calling. He singled out the Green Bay game as mostly ID-based, with some missed run-throughs by blockers. On Jahmyr Gibbs, who leads the NFL in touches, he set no touch limit and said the staff will manage it by communicating with Gibbs, backing off only if Gibbs says he isn't feeling right. He praised Jameson Williams as dynamic and said his confidence hasn't wavered. He also said Jared Goff moved in the pocket as well as he has all season against Green Bay, helping the early explosive plays. Cade Mays' return was called a good start with some rust, and the coach said healthy best players will play. Petzing also joked that he can't dance and is fine with celebrations as long as there is no taunting penalty.

injuries.detail: Listed DNP with an ankle issue on this week's report. Petzing said healthy best players play and called his recent debut after a long layoff a good start with some rust, but gave no status for this week.

signals.claim: Gibbs will keep a heavy workload with no set touch cap, unless he says he isn't feeling good.
signals.note: Gibbs' elite volume looks safe in the short term, though the staff will adjust if he reports fatigue or a physical issue.
signals.quote: it's something you're aware of, you manage

signals.claim: Williams remains a core explosive-play weapon in the offense.
signals.note: After four touchdowns in two weeks, the coordinator describes his play as consistent rather than a hot streak, which supports his weekly ceiling.
signals.quote: He's dynamic. He's explosive. He's fast.

signals.claim: Goff is playing well, moving in the pocket and finding windows, which drove the early explosives against Green Bay.
signals.note: Strong pocket play and protection help the downfield passing game that feeds the Detroit pass catchers.
signals.quote: Jared you know I thought he moved in the pocket

signals.claim: Mays will play if healthy, and his return from the layoff has gone well so far.
signals.note: He is DNP with an ankle issue, so his availability matters for the offensive line and run game against Minnesota's pressure.
signals.quote: as a whole, I thought it was a really good start

topics.detail: Flores runs a system few NFL teams use: identical pre-snap looks, blitzes and drop-outs, and versatile edge rushers (Van Ginkel and Turner) who may rush or drop. Petzing said it creates indecision for quarterbacks and delays throws.

He said the run game has had explosive and negative plays, blaming protection ID and communication, one-on-one losses, and scheme and play-calling. The Green Bay issues were mostly ID-based, with missed run-throughs by blockers.
The run game is 'huge' this week. Petzing wants balance so Minnesota can't predict run or pass.
Petzing called Kyler Murray dynamic with his feet, accurate and strong on quick throws. He said defenders face a big challenge when he extends plays.

title: Eric Bieniemy on the Denver Broncos: 'They're Playing Some Good Ball' | Press Conference 10/29
headline: Bieniemy praised young WR Cyrus Allen and said the 'chains are off' for him, so expect his role to keep growing against Denver after the Seattle loss.
summary: Bieniemy opened by owning the loss at Seattle. He said the offense was outexecuted and outworked in a hostile environment, and that the unit needs to be better prepared mentally and physically. He called it a lesson for a young group, but said distractions such as the Josh Simmons story had nothing to do with the result. He liked Cyrus Allen's game, citing confidence, speed and strong run blocking, while saying every receiver can still clean up route details. He denied the offense is being held back for young players, saying Allen is being put in situations to 'cut it loose.' On Patrick Mahomes, he said the quarterback has grown more patient, takes accountability and handled the frustrating stretches well. He called Denver's defense good and expects them to come out fired up after a poor game. He deflected trade-deadline questions to GM Brett Veach, and said this week's focus is third down, short yardage and goal line. He also said the system asks a lot of receivers, who move around the formation and learn concepts rather than a single spot.

signals.claim: Allen will keep a role in the offense and continue to see an expanding workload.
signals.note: A coordinator who is detail-oriented praised his confidence, speed and run blocking, which supports a growing snap share for the young receiver.
signals.quote: He played with great confidence. He plays fast.

signals.claim: The staff is not holding Allen back and will let him play aggressively in the offense.
signals.note: Bieniemy rejected the idea that the offense is being scaled back for him, which suggests he can be used freely.
signals.quote: the chains are off.

signals.note: Bieniemy was unbothered by the visible frustration in the Seattle game and described Mahomes as more patient and accountable in year ten.
signals.quote: he's not going to make any excuses.

topics.detail: Bieniemy said Seattle executed better and played hungrier. He framed it as a lesson for a young team and said the offense must prepare better for hostile environments.

He called Denver's defense 'playing some good ball' and expects them to come out aggressive after a poor game. He noted a different tempo and intensity when a Denver player named Cooper is on the field.
He deferred to GM Brett Veach on any moves and said he is focused on Denver and situational football: third down, short yardage and goal line.
He said Coach Reid had already addressed it and that it was not a distraction or a factor in the loss. He repeated that the team simply got beat.
The volume of the system is the hardest part for young receivers. They are moved around the formation and must learn concepts and verbiage, since the offense wants to throw it around with Mahomes.

title: Aaron Donald, Puka Nacua & Rams Coordinators speak on scouting the Chargers, takeaways from Week 7 & more
headline: Scheelhaase is leaning on Dylan McMahon at center for Week 8 with Coleman Shelton apparently out, and Colby Parkinson is trusted heavily; Davante Adams' absence is also assumed.
summary: Nate Scheelhaase said the Rams like feeding the ball to different players. He mentioned a past conversation about how Blake Corum and Kyren Williams split reps, and that the last game happened to work out in a particular way. He credited the Week 7 run game on early downs with setting up play action. Matthew Stafford found completions even when defenses took away some of those looks. The longest gain in the last game was only 17 yards, but the offense stayed efficient and ahead of the sticks. He still expects chances for explosive plays. He praised Colby Parkinson as one of the league's best at the point of attack and a growing contributor in the passing game. On the offensive line, he is encouraged by Dylan McMahon, who is replacing Coleman Shelton at center. He called Shelton a key communicator and tone-setter. He described the Chargers defense as big, physical and run-stopping, with Khalil Mack still a disruptive rusher who needs a specific plan. He also said the team still has procedural penalties to clean up.

injuries.detail: The question assumed the Rams must replace him at center on Sunday, and Scheelhaase talked about McMahon filling in. He did not give a formal status or reason.
A reporter said the offense is not having 'Devonte' (taken to mean Adams). Scheelhaase did not dispute it and answered about creating downfield plays without him.

signals.claim: Will keep a significant role as a blocker and pass-game contributor.
signals.note: The coaching staff trusts him with difficult assignments in both phases, which supports steady tight end snaps, though his value leans on blocking.
signals.quote: he's as good as anybody in the league right now at the point of attack

signals.claim: Will play center on Sunday in place of Coleman Shelton.
signals.note: A change at center could affect pass protection and run-blocking consistency against the Chargers' interior.
signals.quote: I'm really encouraged by Dylan McMahon and what he's been able to do

signals.claim: Will not be the starting center on Sunday.
signals.note: His absence removes the offense's center communicator and leader, which could matter for line cohesion.
signals.quote: he's instrumental in everything that we do

signals.claim: Carries and touches in the backfield will be split depending on the game.
signals.note: Scheelhaase kept reps flexible and said the ball finds different players, so Corum's workload is game-dependent.
signals.quote: who ends up in on certain reps

signals.claim: Touches will vary week to week depending on how the game flows.
signals.note: The coordinator described a reps split with Corum rather than a fixed workload, which makes Williams' volume less predictable.
signals.quote: who ends up in on certain reps

topics.detail: Scheelhaase said early-down running made the defense account for the run and set up play action. Even when the Chargers-style coverage took some looks away, Stafford found completions.
The offense's biggest gain last game was 17 yards, yet he felt it was efficient and stayed ahead of the sticks. He believes more downfield chances will come, given how the team is playing.

He called them big, physical and strong up front, ranked near the top in turnovers, third-down defense and red-zone defense. He said Khalil Mack still affects both the pass and run game and needs a plan.
Procedural penalties are down, but two penalties inside the ten-yard line last game were a reminder the team still has a ways to go.

title: Andrew Janocko: 'We don't ever want to copy and paste practice'
headline: Tre Tucker's role is growing and Janocko praised his confidence, while Mike Washington Jr. got no early-down promise and Ashton Jeanty's run game still needs to "trust" what he sees.
summary: Janocko gave mostly general answers on a four-game losing streak, with a road game next. He said the run game, pass game and screens are all being refined daily. On Ashton Jeanty, he said the back needs to trust what he sees, come off the ball and finish plays, and called him a player the offense leans on as both a runner and a receiver. He praised Kirk Cousins's preparation and said Cousins is hard on himself and wants to get Jalen Nailor, Brock Bowers and the other skill players more involved. He called Tre Tucker confident and said his opportunities are earned, in a room where everyone is pushed to add to their skill set. On Bowers, he said heavy defensive attention is expected and the offense adjusts to whatever coverages or wrinkles teams show. He gave Mike Washington Jr. no promise of early-down work, saying more opportunities will follow his improvement. He also said Kubiak changes practice each week to simulate harder game situations and fix recent shortfalls, and that the staff scouts itself honestly after games to decide between adjusting and sticking with its identity.

injuries.detail: Late in the session Janocko said a player is getting back into his groove after an injury and will be monitored over the next days and weeks. The name is not clear in the captions. The injury report lists Ian Thomas (ankle, full practice) and Trey Zuhn (concussion, limited), and either could fit, so no one is named.

signals.claim: Tucker will keep an expanded role beyond conventional speed usage as he earns opportunities.
signals.note: A confident, trending receiver with an expanding role could see more targets, though Janocko gave no specifics.
signals.quote: somebody that's playing with a lot of confidence

signals.claim: Jeanty remains a featured piece as both runner and receiver, and needs to trust his reads and finish runs.
signals.note: His rushing efficiency has lagged, but the coach says he is a focal point and his pass-catching keeps his volume safe.
signals.quote: we lean on as our in our offense

signals.claim: Cousins and Nailor are working on getting Nailor more chances after Cousins missed him open on tape.
signals.note: Possible target upside for Nailor, but Janocko framed it as general improvement and did not commit to a bigger role.
signals.quote: he wants the best for his teammates and the best for everybody around him

signals.claim: Bowers will keep drawing heavy defensive attention and the offense will adjust to coverages and wrinkles.
signals.note: Heavy attention can cap his volume in some matchups, but it also opens targets for others.
signals.quote: teams play coverages, teams play their schemes

signals.claim: Washington's opportunities will grow as he improves, but no specific early-down role was committed.
signals.note: He may see more work if his production continues, but Janocko did not commit to early downs.
signals.quote: as that happened, then more opportunities will come

topics.detail: Kubiak changes practice each week to simulate game situations that are as hard as or harder than games, and targets areas where the team fell short or can capitalize. Janocko said the staff does not want to copy and paste practice.
Asked about frustration during a four-game losing streak, Janocko pointed to the team's character and belief, and said the staff will keep working until results come.
The staff reviews one-game and seven-game samples after games to decide what to build on and what to fix before the next opponent.
Janocko said Thornton is working every day to take advantage of his reps and earn an opportunity in the offense. Thornton is not on the provided roster, so no signal was created.

A player Janocko referred to as Preston (the name is not clear in the captions) is working on communication with the line, and Janocko said the linemen and backs are always talking in meetings and walkthroughs.

title: Sean Mannion Press Conference: October 29, 2026
headline: With the running back room banged up, Mannion is confident in Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell stepping in, while Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers are growing into bigger roles and the line gets Dickerson and Kendall back.
summary: Mannion opened by addressing the thinned-out running back room. He said the staff coaches every player on the roster, so Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue can step in and be productive. He called Mitchell a proven back and Blue an exciting young talent who improves weekly. He praised Makai Lemon's catch-and-run ability and growing confidence, and said Eli Stowers handled his first NFL game action and can play several roles. Overall he thought the offense executed much more cleanly in the last game, citing communication, third downs, red-zone finishing and receiver blocking, and he plans to keep the extra Monday film session. He said Tanner McKee has improved steadily, that Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall returning gave the line a boost, and that Markel Bell keeps gaining confidence. He called new backup QB Joe Milton III talented but still catching up on the playbook. He closed by previewing a rematch with a well-coached Washington defense on Sunday night.

injuries.detail: Back on the offensive line after missing time. Mannion said getting him and Drew Kendall back together was big for the line's communication and confidence.
Returned to the offensive line mix alongside Dickerson and was praised as a great communicator.
Played his first NFL game action. Mannion said he is still catching up on reps lost to injury.

signals.claim: Blue will step into the depleted running back rotation and be productive.
signals.note: With the backfield injuries, Blue is in line for real touches and the coordinator is publicly confident in him.
signals.quote: he's an exciting young talent.

signals.claim: Mitchell will play a role in the running back rotation this week.
signals.note: A veteran with a productive track record, he is a likely beneficiary of the injuries at running back.
signals.quote: Elijah's been a really, really productive back in this league.

signals.claim: Lemon's production will keep growing as he gets more full-speed reps.
signals.note: Mannion singled out his catch-and-run skills after the Cowboys game, and his confidence and reps are still building.
signals.quote: his confidence grows every time he steps out there.

signals.claim: Stowers will keep playing multiple roles at tight end as he gets more reps.
signals.note: The coaches are comfortable using him in several roles after his debut, so he is a tight end to watch as his snaps grow.
signals.quote: he did everything we asked of him.

signals.claim: McKee continues to operate as the starting quarterback with improving command of the offense.
signals.note: Mannion praised his decision-making and week-to-week growth, which supports the offense's efficiency.
signals.quote: Tanner made good decisions with the football.

signals.claim: Bell keeps developing as a run blocker and pass protector on the offensive line.
signals.note: His improvement and the line's return to health should help the run game and protection.
signals.quote: his confidence continues to grow.

signals.claim: Dickerson is back in the lineup and the line is more settled with him in.
signals.note: A healthier, more experienced line is good for the run game and for QB protection.
signals.quote: Landon's a great communicator. Drew's a great communicator.

signals.claim: Kendall is back in the lineup with the other starters up front.
signals.note: His return helps line communication and stability.
signals.quote: Drew's a great communicator.

signals.claim: Milton is the backup quarterback and is still catching up on the playbook.
signals.note: He is not a fantasy factor unless the starting quarterback situation changes, but he is the next man up.
signals.quote: you can see things to be really excited about.

signals.claim: The screen game will continue to be part of the offense, with Cooper as a recipient.
signals.note: Screens are producing yards after the catch for him and the offensive line is blocking them well.
signals.quote: coop kind of took it cross country on that one.

topics.detail: The team may be down to its sixth and seventh running backs. Mannion said the staff coaches every roster member, so replacements are mentally ready and the depth has been a luxury during these injuries.

Mannion said the offense was much cleaner in the last game, with better communication, third-down conversions, red-zone finishing and physical running. The slow starts were attributed to small fundamentals, and he called out receiver blocking in the run game.
The full offense met for a Monday film session to show how the position groups work together. He called it productive and likely to continue when the schedule permits.
The screen game worked because of sound line fundamentals: setting the hook, getting defensive linemen to rush upfield, taking proper angles and finishing downfield with effort.

title: Zac Robinson on Familiarity of Facing the Falcons | Press Conference
headline: Tampa Bay's run-heavy offense (58 handoffs) is working, Tez Johnson's role is growing with Jalen McMillan out, and the tight ends will keep getting run-game work, but Sunday's matchup with Atlanta's strong run defense and secondary may force more balance.
summary: Robinson called the offense's run-game performance outstanding and said it took all 11 players, with the line setting the table and the tight ends and receivers blocking well. He said Baker Mayfield's third-down conversions and his run-game checks at the line were key. He also said it was great to have Mayfield back, and the team handed the ball off 58 times. He praised Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell (a big run) and Sean Tucker (late-game speed through creases). Looking ahead to Atlanta, he stressed balance against a good run defense and a strong secondary, called A.J. Terrell excellent and the safety tandem possibly the league's best, and said weather could change the plan. Robinson was on Atlanta's staff, so there is some familiarity, but both rosters and schemes have changed. He raised Tez Johnson's profile, citing his speed, his mental handling of a high-volume role and his blocking, and said they want to keep elevating his role with Jalen McMillan ("Jmax") down. He also praised the tight ends in 12 and 13 personnel, singling out Cade Otton's blocking and Bauer Sharp's physicality, and said Sharp should keep getting opportunities.

injuries.detail: Robinson said Tez Johnson's role has grown "since Jmax been down," so McMillan is currently sidelined. No return timeline was given.
Robinson said it was great having Mayfield back for the Carolina game, which implies he was recently out or limited. No current concern was raised.

signals.claim: Mayfield is back as the starter and is making run-game checks and key third-down plays.
signals.note: Mayfield is healthy and trusted at the line of scrimmage, but a run-heavy game script (11 pass attempts) caps his passing volume.
signals.quote: it was great having him back

signals.claim: Irving remains part of a productive run-heavy rotation that the team wants to keep balanced.
signals.note: Strong blocking and a heavy run share help the backs, though the carries are split among several runners.
signals.quote: And the runners ran outstanding.

signals.claim: Gainwell is a contributing runner who produced a big breakaway run.
signals.note: He is a rotational back with upside, but his role compared with Irving's is not defined.
signals.quote: Kenny had a huge run there.

signals.claim: Tucker can break long runs when given a crease late in games.
signals.note: He is a speed option behind the main backs, and late-game usage in a lead is his path to carries.
signals.quote: his speed shows up when he's got a crease

signals.claim: Johnson's snaps and role in the passing game will keep increasing while McMillan is out.
signals.note: He is an explosive deep threat with growing trust, and his role is expanding with the injuries at receiver.
signals.quote: We just got to keep, you know, elevating his role as much as we can

signals.claim: Sharp will keep getting opportunities as a physical blocker in multi-tight-end sets.
signals.note: He is a run-game-oriented tight end, so his value is mostly blocking snaps and his fantasy upside is limited.
signals.quote: So we got to keep giving him ops.

signals.claim: Otton remains a core tight end in 11, 12 and 13 personnel and is valued for his blocking.
signals.note: He is trusted in every package, but the usage points more toward blocking than targets.
signals.quote: he's a great blocker

signals.claim: Durham is part of the 12 and 13 personnel groupings the offense uses to run the ball.
signals.note: Heavy tight end sets tend to reduce wide receiver snaps and targets.
signals.quote: I love the way that those guys have been playing at the tight end spot

signals.claim: McMillan has been down for some time and his role has been filled by Tez Johnson.
signals.note: He is out with no timeline given, which keeps Johnson in a bigger role.

topics.detail: The offense handed the ball off 58 times, kept moving the chains on early downs and set the tone with the opening drive. Robinson said it took all 11 players, including receivers and tight ends blocking. Ted Hurst's block on a safety sprung a run on the second play.

Robinson expects a physical game against a team with strong players at all three levels. He called A.J. Terrell excellent and the safety tandem possibly the league's best. The front plays a different style than the one Tampa Bay just faced.
Robinson wants balance on offense, but weather on Sunday could change the plan. He noted that some weeks bring fewer run opportunities and you have to adjust.

Robinson coached on Atlanta's staff in 2025 and practiced against them. He said both teams have changed personnel and schemes, so there is only some carryover. He spoke warmly of Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr.'s talent and resilience.
